requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation. No marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics/housing) when approved as an ESA type: R10 approval mark per paragraph 5.3. present. Pass if present; not required where the electronics are approved only as part of a vehicle type.

requirements.text: Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspection of the ESA marking per paragraph 5.3. on the uninstalled lamp; confirm the marking is present on the ESA. Its visibility when the lamp is installed on the vehicle is not required, so the check passes even if the marking is hidden.

requirements.text: A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Design review plus vehicle-level and ESA-level EMC testing per UN R10. Pass if the vehicle, with the lamp fitted and operated in normal conditions of use, meets all R10 emission and immunity requirements.

requirements.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions.
requirements.test_case: ESA broadband and narrowband radiated emission tests per Annexes 7 and 8, with the rear position, stop and reversing functions operating. Pass if the emissions are within the R10 ESA limits.

requirements.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.
requirements.test_case: ESA conducted transient emission test on supply lines per Annex 10, with each lamp function switched. Pass if the transients are within the R10 limits.

requirements.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
requirements.test_case: ESA radiated immunity test per Annex 9 (e.g. ALSE, TEM cell, BCI or stripline) at the specified field strength. Pass if the rear position, stop and reversing lamps show no flicker or loss of function beyond the pass/fail criteria in the test plan.

requirements.text: ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: ESA conducted transient immunity test on supply lines per Annex 10, using the specified test pulses. Pass if the lamp functions meet the required functional status for each pulse.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
requirements.test_case: Annex 7 broadband measurement, 30-75 MHz; pass if measured values are below the logarithmically decreasing limit from 62 to 52 dBµV/m (Appendix 6).

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.test_case: Annex 7 broadband measurement, 400-1,000 MHz; pass if measured values are below 63 dBµV/m.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Annex 7 broadband measurement over 30-1,000 MHz with each lamp function (rear position, stop, reversing) operating; pass if all measured values are below the limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
requirements.test_case: Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission scan 30-75 MHz; pass if emissions are below the limit line falling logarithmically from 52 to 42 dBµV/m (Appendix 7).

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
requirements.test_case: Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission scan 400-1,000 MHz; pass if emissions are below 53 dBµV/m.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Compare Annex 8 narrowband results for the representative lamp, rear position, stop and reversing functions each active, against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits over 30-1,000 MHz; pass if all values are below the limits.

requirements.text: For ESAs on vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances emitted on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
requirements.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 transient emission measurement at 12 V supply, including switching of the rear position, stop and reversing functions; pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

requirements.text: When tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 60 V/m; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions over at least 90 % of the band.

requirements.text: When tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 50 V/m; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions at any frequency.

requirements.text: When tested by the bulk current injection (BCI) method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 BCI test, 20 to 400 MHz at 60 mA injected current; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions over at least 90 % of the band.

requirements.text: When tested by the bulk current injection (BCI) method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 BCI test, 20 to 400 MHz at 50 mA; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions at any frequency.

requirements.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 21 V/m; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions over at least 90 % of the band.

requirements.text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be immune at a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
requirements.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 18 V/m; pass if no degradation of immunity related functions at any frequency.

requirements.text: The ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".
requirements.test_case: During all Annex 9 immunity tests, monitor light output of rear position, stop and reversing functions (no unintended switching, flicker, extinguishing or intensity change); pass if no degradation of immunity related functions observed.

requirements.text: Starting profile (applicable only to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor): at immunity test level II for 12 V systems and level II for 24 V systems, 10 pulses, an ESA related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases shall achieve functional status B.
requirements.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II (12 V), 10 pulses, with lamp functions activated; pass if functional status B per ISO 16750-1 (lamp functions may deviate during test but return to normal automatically afterwards).

requirements.text: Starting profile (applicable only to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor): at immunity test level II for 12 V systems and level II for 24 V systems, 10 pulses, other ESAs related to immunity related functions shall achieve functional status C.
requirements.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses; pass if functional status C per ISO 16750-1.

requirements.text: Test pulse 1 at -75 V for 12 V systems (-450 V for 24 V systems), 500 pulses: ESA functions related to immunity related functions shall achieve FPSC III.
requirements.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 1, -75 V (12 V system), 500 pulses; pass if FPSC III per ISO 7637-1.

requirements.text: Test pulse 3a at -112 V for 12 V systems (-150 V for 24 V systems), test duration 1 h: ESA functions related to immunity related functions shall achieve FPSC I.
requirements.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a, -112 V (12 V system), 1 h; pass if FPSC I.

requirements.text: Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
requirements.test_case: Design review of the PCB schematic and BOM: confirm absence of any oscillator, switching regulator or PWM source with operating frequency > 9 kHz. If confirmed, the narrowband emission tests (para. 6.3.2./6.6.2., Annexes 5 and 8) are waived. Otherwise perform the Annex 8 narrowband test.

requirements.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Function analysis of the ESA against the immunity related functions list (e.g. signalling functions such as stop lamp). If no immunity related function is present, Annex 9 radiated immunity testing is waived. Otherwise perform the Annex 9 test with no change of lamp state (stop/position/reversing) under exposure.

requirements.text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Design review of the ESA circuit: confirm the ESA is not switched, contains no switches or contains no inductive load. If confirmed, the Annex 10 transient conducted emission test is waived. Otherwise perform the transient emission test on the 12/24 V supply lines against the limits of para. 6.7.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiated emissions of the ESA (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), in the frequency range 30-75 MHz, shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions per the method referenced by paragraph 6.5.2.1./7.10.2.1. (Annex 7 ESA method) with 120 kHz bandwidth, lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) operating; across 30-75 MHz, pass if measured level ≤ 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at every frequency.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiated emissions of the ESA (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz, shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions per the method referenced by paragraph 6.5.2.1./7.10.2.1. (Annex 7 ESA method) with 120 kHz bandwidth, lamp functions operating; across 400-1,000 MHz, pass if measured level ≤ 63 dBµV/m at every frequency.

requirements.text: For an ESA, the narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission in the frequency range 30-75 MHz shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation).
requirements.test_case: Narrowband radiated emission measurement of the ESA per paragraph 6.6.2.1. (Annex 8 method), 120 kHz bandwidth, 30-75 MHz, with all lamp functions operating; pass if every measured level is at or below 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

requirements.text: For an ESA, the narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation).
requirements.test_case: Narrowband radiated emission measurement of the ESA per paragraph 6.6.2.1. (Annex 8 method), 120 kHz bandwidth, 400-1,000 MHz, with all lamp functions operating; pass if every measured level is at or below 53 dBµV/m.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Radiated emission scan 30-1,000 MHz in ALSE/OATS; pass if emissions below para 6.5 broadband ESA limits across the full range

requirements.text: Measurements can be performed with either quasi-peak or peak detectors; the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. are for quasi-peak detectors, and if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Verify detector type in report; if peak detector, check 20 dB correction applied to limits per CISPR 12

requirements.text: For purely broadband disturbances, the maximum frequency step size of the scanning receiver may be increased up to a value not greater than the bandwidth value; for emissions generated by brush commutator motors without an electronic control unit, the maximum step size may be increased up to five times the bandwidth.
requirements.test_case: Verify step size used does not exceed bandwidth (or 5 × bandwidth for brush commutator motors without ECU)

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Annex 8 test with all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) energised in normal operation at maximum load; pass if the operating state is documented as normal/maximum load.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Radiated narrowband scan 30-1,000 MHz in ALSE/OATS; pass if the emissions are below the paragraph 6.6.2.1. limits across the whole range.

requirements.text: Narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Check the receiver configuration; pass if the average detector is used.

requirements.text: ESAs may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11. Frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports: the chosen ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps. Pass if there is no gap in coverage.

requirements.text: ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Sweep 20–6,000 MHz with step sizes per ISO 11452-1. Pass if the lamp functions show no malfunction across the whole range.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Verify the signal generator settings: AM at 1 kHz with 80 % depth for 20–400 MHz. Pass if the ESA is immune with these settings.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Verify the generator settings: PM with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs for 2,700–3,100 MHz. Pass if the ESA is immune.

requirements.text: The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Verify the generator settings: PM with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs for 380–2,700 MHz and 3,100–6,000 MHz. Pass if the ESA is immune.

requirements.text: As an alternative, the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the BCI substitution method and the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Perform in-vehicle BCI per ISO 11451-4 with the probe at 150 mm from the lamp. Pass if there is no malfunction.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as ensured by the test method of Annex 10.
requirements.test_case: Annex 10 transient immunity tests (paragraph 2): ESA functions as required with no unacceptable degradation of the lamp functions

requirements.text: Conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, as ensured by the test method of Annex 10.
requirements.test_case: Annex 10 transient emission measurement (paragraph 3): emitted transients within the specified limits

requirements.text: Test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines, and the ESA shall be immune to these transient disturbances.
requirements.test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b applied to supply lines and connections operationally connected to them; pass: ESA meets its functional status requirements

requirements.text: The starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines, and the ESA shall be immune to it; ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.
requirements.test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile applied to supply lines and operationally connected connections (unless ESA exclusively for electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor); pass: ESA meets its functional status requirements

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of drawings and samples: a marking area exists that accommodates the approval marking and all markings of 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.

requirements.text: All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visual check of legibility; indelibility check (e.g. rubbing test with water/solvent-soaked cloth); markings remain legible.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension "a" of the approval mark per Annex 7 arrangement; pass if a ≥ 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of marking: circle around "E" with distinguishing number of approving country present.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., and this sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: 4–6 digit sequential number present and located adjacent to the approval mark.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: function symbols per 3.2.4 present for each approved function (e.g. R, S1, AR).

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by two-digit series of amendments present.

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: Check whether lamp is handed; if so, verify horizontal mounting arrow present on marking.

requirements.text: For front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps which cannot be mounted on either side indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of fitted lamp/drawing: arrow points outboard of vehicle.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: if reversing lamp approved with reduced distribution as a pair, arrow points outboard.

requirements.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: "D" to the right of the function symbol where lamp is approved as part of two independent lamps.

requirements.text: If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: "Y" to the right of the function symbol where lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system.

requirements.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: downward vertical arrow from horizontal segment present where reduced light distribution approved.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of lamp sample: complete approval marking present.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: applicant trade name or mark present on lamp.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with: (a) an electronic light source control gear; and/or (b) a variable luminous intensity control; and/or (c) a secondary operating mode; and/or (d) non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: rated voltage (e.g. 12V) or voltage range marked on lamp when any of conditions (a)-(d) apply.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of module: applicant trade name or mark present.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1., followed by additional symbols or characters in case several non-identical light source modules are used; the approval mark does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: module code "MD" + approval mark without circle (+ distinguishing characters for non-identical modules); verify same applicant as lamp mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: rated voltage or range marked on module.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: module identification code marked on lamp matches module.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: rated voltage or range marked on lamp.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of external control gear: identification number and manufacturer name present.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Design review: marking located on a part permanently attached to the light-emitting outer lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Inspection on vehicle: marking visible as fitted or after opening boot lid/door/hood.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: If lens is detachable, verify approval marking on both lens and housing.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Where lens is shared, verify each housing bears only its own function approval markings.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: listed markings located on the lamp itself.

requirements.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed anywhere on the lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: If single mark used: inspect on vehicle that mark is visible after installation.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is used on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Design review/disassembly: removal of any light-transmitting part also removes the approval mark.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure mark components; compare with minimum sizes in each applicable Regulation; pass if ≥ the smallest individual required size.

requirements.text: Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
requirements.test_case: Review the conformity assessment against every applicable requirement of paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R148 for each lamp function submitted. Pass if all applicable requirements are met and none is unaddressed.

requirements.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp; the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: At lamp type approval, identify the applicable sections 5 and 6 requirements of UN R48 (series in force) for each function (rear position, stop, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector) and vehicle category M1. Verify the requirements that can be checked at lamp level, e.g. geometric visibility angles (reversing lamp to 45° outboard), colour and number of lamps, against the lamp design and installation drawings. Pass if all feasible-to-verify requirements are met.

requirements.text: The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Design verification: vibration test representative of vehicle use (e.g. per manufacturer/OEM vibration profile) on the complete rear combination lamp, followed by functional check and re-measurement of photometric and colorimetric characteristics; pass if all functions operate satisfactorily and still meet the R148 photometric and colour requirements.

requirements.text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.
requirements.test_case: Document and marking review: confirm that any lamp function marked "Y" is one of the listed functions (e.g. rear position or stop lamp), not the reversing lamp or retro-reflector. Pass if no "Y" marking is applied to non-listed functions.

requirements.text: Front and rear position lamps which are grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated may also be used as end-outline marker lamps.
requirements.test_case: Design review: if the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated rear position lamp is used as an end-outline marker lamp, confirm it meets the rear position lamp approval.

requirements.text: Position lamps or daytime running lamps which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, are permitted.
requirements.test_case: Design and photometric review: where the rear position lamp shares an LED source with another function, verify the intensity regulation system operates permanently and photometry is met in each mode.

requirements.text: In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source); or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Design review of LED circuit: verify separate light sources for rear position and stop functions, or verify the vehicle provides a failure tell-tale for the lamps; pass if one of the alternatives is met.

requirements.text: The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo, built by transparent or non-transparent components, provided that all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation are fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: count logos within the apparent surface (max one) and verify full photometric/colour compliance of the function with the logo present.

requirements.text: Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed within the apparent surface of a lamp (function).
requirements.test_case: Inspection of logo content and applicant statement per paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f); pass if logo is the vehicle or body manufacturer brand name only.

requirements.text: The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of such a lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure projected enclosed logo area in the direction of the reference axis; pass if ≤ 100 cm2.

requirements.text: Notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
requirements.test_case: Design review: logo asymmetry accepted; verify remaining symmetry requirements of the lamp installation are met.

requirements.text: Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp apparent surface and outer lens; pass if no logo is present.

requirements.text: Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp apparent surface and outer lens; pass if no logo is present.

requirements.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Review of the circuit diagram and LED wiring (series strings) per function. Each group wired so that one LED failure extinguishes the whole group is treated as one light source in the failure assessment of paragraph 4.6.1.2.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
requirements.test_case: Option (a): simulate failure of each light source (or group per para 4.6.1.1) in turn. Measure on a goniophotometer at the Annex 3 standard light distribution points. Pass if every point is at or above the minimum, and if the maximum intensities are not exceeded with all light sources lit. Option (b): simulate each failure and verify that a tell-tale activation signal per the cited UN R48 paragraphs is output at the connector, and that the communication form carries the note.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Applies if the position lamp is category R2. Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the photometry. Pass if the lamp automatically reverts to the steady luminous intensity requirements of the respective category, with no emission above the R1 maximum.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with: replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Design review of the bill of materials and light source documentation: every light source is a UN R37/R99/R128 approved replaceable light source without use restriction, a light source module, or a non-replaceable light source; any other light source type is a fail.

requirements.text: Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: EMC testing of radiated and conducted (power line) emissions at vehicle-type level, e.g. per UN R10. Pass if no malfunction of other vehicle electric/electronic systems is caused.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Fitting test: attempt to install the module in alternative positions and orientations. Pass if it fits only in the designated and correct position.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Removal test: attempt to remove the module by hand without tools. Pass if removal is possible only with tool(s).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspection and tamper attempt on the module construction. Pass if it cannot be opened or modified without visible destruction.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.
requirements.test_case: Interchangeability check: attempt to fit UN approved replaceable light sources in the module seat, with and without tools. Pass if none can be fitted.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Interchangeability check: attempt to swap modules of different characteristics between seats in the same housing, with and without tools. Pass if no swap is possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another sample bearing the same identification code, then repeat the photometric measurements per UN R148. Pass if all photometric requirements are met.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure with steady (continuous) operation; verify that no flashing or pulsed mode is used unless specified.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
requirements.test_case: Apply 13.5 V (12 V system) or the applicable value at the lamp terminals; verify the voltage during the photometric test.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp per the applicant's specification with the control gear supplied if required; record the operating conditions.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate per the applicant's specified voltage or current; verify the conditions in the test report.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Annex 3/Annex 8: measure HV on both samples; pass if ≥ the paragraph 5. minimum.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Scan the full visible field on both samples; pass if no value exceeds the paragraph 5. maximum.

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction in question.
requirements.test_case: Measure each Annex 3 grid point; pass if ≥ minimum × % (or ≥ the specified value).

requirements.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure at the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles (e.g. reversing lamp to 45° outboard); pass if ≥ the specified minimum.

requirements.text: The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the local intensity variations per Annex 3 criteria.

requirements.text: In order to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No. 48, the applicant may request an additional test to show that in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction the maximum intensity is not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd; this additional test may be conducted taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.
requirements.test_case: Optional test: measure over H 165°–180° outboard and V -2.5° to +5°; pass if max ≤ 0.25 cd.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Drive the control through all states; pass if the intensities stay within the paragraph 5. range.

requirements.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp: (a) for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, under night-time conditions; (b) for other systems, under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens).
requirements.test_case: Set the night-time or standard condition; pass if the measured intensity is ≤ the steady maximum.

requirements.text: If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table; if one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered are those obtained with all sources in operation.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop+position and position alone over ±5° V / ±10° H; pass if the ratio is ≥ 5:1 at each point.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visual/colorimetric inspection of emitted light outside the Annex 3 grid field for each function; pass if no sharp colour variation is observed.

requirements.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric verification of the complete lamp with its built-in LED modules operated per relevant subparagraphs of 4.8; chromaticity within the function's colour limits.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of rear position lamps (R1, R2, MR) and rear end-outline marker lamps (RM1, RM2) shall meet the requirements in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1. and Annex 3 Figure A3-I / Table A2-1; pass if all Table 4 values are met by each sample.

requirements.text: Rear position lamps of category R1 or MR, and rear end-outline marker lamps of category RM1 (steady), shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)), with the standard light distribution defined by Figure A3-I and Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on axis and at the Figure A3-I / Table A2-1 grid points; pass if the minimum is >= 4 cd and the distribution percentages are met.

requirements.text: Rear position lamps of category R1 or MR, and rear end-outline marker lamps of category RM1 (steady), shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement over the distribution field; pass if the maximum is <= 17 cd.

requirements.text: Rear position lamps of category R1 or MR, and rear end-outline marker lamps of category RM1 (steady), shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.5∙10^0 cd for a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2., Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the lamp marked "D"; pass if the maximum is <= 8.5 cd.

requirements.text: Rear position lamps of category R1 or MR, and rear end-outline marker lamps of category RM1 (steady), shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)).
requirements.test_case: Measurement at the boundaries and within the angles of geometric visibility; pass if every value is >= 0.05 cd.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the rear position function below 5° down from horizontal; pass if the intensity is <= 60 cd there and the Table 4 maximum is met elsewhere.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by rear position lamps (R1, R2, MR) and rear end-outline marker lamps (RM1, RM2) shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light; pass if the chromaticity coordinates are within the red boundaries of the colour definition referenced by the Regulation.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of stop lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7 for its category (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS).
requirements.test_case: Photometric goniometer measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1; pass if all Table 7 values for the declared category are met on each sample.

requirements.text: A category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a)).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement on reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(a); pass if ≥ 60 cd on both samples.

requirements.text: A category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60·10^2 cd when used as a single lamp, or 1.30·10^2 cd for a lamp marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.) (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b)).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement over the distribution per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(b); pass if max ≤ 260 cd (single) or ≤ 130 cd (marked D).

requirements.text: A category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall meet the standard light distribution defined in Table A2-1 (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c)).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the Table A2-1 grid points per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(c); pass if all point values are met.

requirements.text: A category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 3·10^-1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d)).
requirements.test_case: Measure over the Figure A3-I geometric visibility field per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if ≥ 0.3 cd everywhere.

requirements.text: A category S2 (variable) stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I of 3·10^-1 cd (day) and 7·10^-2 cd (night) (paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d)).
requirements.test_case: Measure over the Figure A3-I field in day and night modes per paragraph 4.8.3.1.(d); pass if ≥ 0.3 cd (day) and ≥ 0.07 cd (night).

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of emitted light through the outer lens; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the red boundaries of the regulation.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of reversing lamp (AR) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10: minimum luminous intensity 8.0∙10^1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(a)) according to the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V (par. 4.8.3.1.(c)).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement on both samples per par. 4.8.3.1. and Figure A3-V; all grid points meet minimum 80 cd scaled per standard light distribution.

requirements.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the h-plane.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on both samples in or above H-plane; max intensity ≤ 300 cd.

requirements.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed 6.00∙10^2 cd below the h-plane, down to 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on both samples between H and 5°D; max intensity ≤ 600 cd.

requirements.text: The maximum luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on both samples below 5°D; max intensity ≤ 8000 cd.

requirements.text: In the case where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied; the device shall then only be installed in a pair.
requirements.test_case: If pair-only approval claimed: photometric measurement up to 30° inwards; intensity at 30° inwards ≥ 25 cd; verify vehicle installation is in pairs.

requirements.text: The failure provisions of paragraph 4.6. shall apply to the reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify compliance with par. 4.6 failure provisions (e.g., LED failure simulation) for the reversing function.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of emitted light; chromaticity coordinates within white boundaries defined by the regulation.

requirements.text: Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Conformity of production check: compare production samples with the approved type (drawings, photometry, colour, markings); pass if no deviation from the approved type.

requirements.text: For conformity of production, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of production samples at the prescribed test points per Annex 2/3; pass if each measured value deviates unfavourably by no more than 20 % from the prescribed value.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12: required minimum 7∙10-1 cd → 5∙10-1 cd (20 per cent) / 3∙10-1 cd (30 per cent); 6∙10-1 cd → 4∙10-1 cd / 2∙10-1 cd; 3∙10-1 cd → 2∙10-1 cd / 1∙10-1 cd; 7∙10-2 cd → 5∙10-2 cd / 3∙10-2 cd; 5∙10-2 cd → 3∙10-2 cd / 2∙10-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3 on production samples; pass if measured values are not below the Table 12 equivalent 20 per cent (or 30 per cent where applicable under Annex 5) values.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility shown in Annex 2 are correct for lamps to be mounted on the right side of the vehicle; for lamps mounted on the left side the angles shall be applied mirror-symmetrically (inboard/outboard interchanged).
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 on right- and left-hand variants; verify inboard/outboard angles are applied relative to the vehicle side of mounting.

requirements.text: Front/rear position lamps (A, R1, R2) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard; reduced angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify unobstructed apparent surface over 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° below H-plane if H-plane < 750 mm).

requirements.text: Front/rear position lamps (A, R1, R2) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below; 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1 at the declared mounting height: verify vertical angles 15°/15° (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm; 5°/15° if > 2,100 mm).

requirements.text: Front/rear position lamps singular (MA, MR) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 80° inboard / 80° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 80°/80° horizontal visibility.

requirements.text: Front/rear position lamps singular (MA, MR) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 10° below, or 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 15°/10° vertical (15°/5° if H-plane < 750 mm).

requirements.text: Stop lamps singular (MS) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Geometric visibility measurement per Annex 2 Table A2-1: verify 45°/45° horizontal visibility.

requirements.text: Unless specified otherwise, the light intensity in the various directions of measurement shall meet the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, these values being mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis (on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement relative to the reference axis and centre of reference at the grid points of the applicable Annex 3 figure; pass if each measured intensity >= the figure's percentage × required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: Where front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS, or side marker lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the manufacturer-declared mounting height (H plane); if <= 750 mm, verify photometric intensity down to V = 5° down only; pass if all points from 5° down upward meet the minimums.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern should be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
requirements.test_case: Scan intensity between grid points of the applicable figure; pass if every intermediate direction >= the lowest minimum value on the surrounding grid lines.

requirements.text: In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of a lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
requirements.test_case: Visual examination of the lit reversing lamp; if local variations appear, measure intensity between adjacent measuring directions of Figure A3-V; pass if every value >= 50 % of the lower of the two prescribed minimums.

requirements.text: Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement at the Figure A3-I grid points; pass if each intensity >= the stated percentage of the minimum required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 for the respective function.

requirements.text: Reversing lamps shall meet, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference (H = 0°, V = 0°, on the vehicle horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference), the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing lamp at the Figure A3-V measuring points; pass if each intensity >= the cd value shown in Figure A3-V.

requirements.text: With respect to photometric performance, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Photometric test per paragraph 4.8. on a randomly selected production lamp; pass if no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of randomly selected production lamps under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.; pass if chromaticity coordinates are within the prescribed limits.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements. The luminous intensity distribution after 1 and after 10 minutes of operation may be calculated from the distribution measured after photometric stability by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 minute, after 10 minutes and after photometric stability has occurred.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp from cold switch-on at 1 min and 10 min (directly, or scaled from the stabilized distribution by the HV ratios); pass if all test points are within the min/max intensity limits at both times.

requirements.text: For all lamps other than reversing and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements. The luminous intensity distribution after 1 min of operation may be calculated from the distribution after 30 min of operation or after photometric stabilization by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 min and after 30 min or after photometric stabilization.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of rear position and stop functions at 1 min and at 30 min or after photometric stability (direct, or 1 min distribution scaled by HV ratio); pass if all test points are within the min/max limits.

requirements.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the front and rear position lamp shall additionally be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate; the distribution at that point in time may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV at 4 s after switch ON and scale the paragraph 1 distribution; pass if all test points meet the min/max requirements (deemed compliant for LED-only per paragraph 2.1.2).

requirements.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm by design documentation that each function uses LED light sources only; pass if paragraph 1.2 measurements are compliant.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Drawing/sample inspection: verify a reserved marking area of sufficient size exists for UI or approval marking plus paragraph 3.3.4.2. markings.

requirements.text: All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection for legibility; indelibility check (e.g. rub test with water/solvent cloth); pass if markings remain legible.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value for "a" defined in Table 1; the arrangement of the markings may follow the examples shown in Annex 10.
requirements.test_case: Measure approval mark dimensions against Table 1 value of "a"; compare layout with Annex 10.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of marking on sample: circle with "E" and country number present.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: 4–6 digit sequential number present and located adjacent to the approval mark, matching the approval number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: class identification symbol per paragraph 3.2.5. present and correct for the approved class.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection: "150R" followed by two-digit series of amendments present.

requirements.text: The approval marking as defined in paragraph 3.3.2. may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; where used, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: If UI used: visual comparison of mark with Figure I format; UI number matches UN database entry.

requirements.text: Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of sample for applicant trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Review manufacturer's prescribed rotation angles; if orientation ambiguous, verify "TOP" inscribed horizontally at highest part of illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of device: approval marking/UI, trade name and TOP marking (where required) legible.

requirements.text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1. and 3.3.6.1.2. are met.
requirements.test_case: Inspect combined lamp marking: single mark contains sequential number/UI and conditions 3.3.6.1.1–3.3.6.1.2 satisfied.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is used on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.test_case: Install lamp on vehicle/representative fixture; verify single approval mark visible.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is used on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
requirements.test_case: Design review/disassembly: verify each light-transmitting part cannot be removed without removing the approval mark (e.g. mark on outer lens).

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure mark components; compare against the minimum sizes of each pertinent UN Regulation; pass if not below the smallest required.

requirements.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
requirements.test_case: Production samples tested to the photometric, colorimetric and other requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5.; pass if samples meet all requirements and conform to the approved type.

requirements.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflecting device; the requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Document and design review against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes (series of amendments in force at application) for the rear retro-reflector on category M1: e.g. installation position (height, lateral, distance to edge), geometric visibility angles, orientation, number and colour. Pass: all requirements verifiable at device approval are met.

requirements.text: Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Design review and conformity tests of UN R150 (photometric, environmental and durability tests); device keeps meeting photometric requirements after the tests.

requirements.text: Retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection and design/manufacturing review of samples; no defect affecting operation or maintenance found.

requirements.text: The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Manual dismantling attempt without tools on the assembled lamp; retro-reflector components cannot be easily separated.

requirements.text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspection of the outer surface and cleaning trial with cloth; surface can be easily cleaned.

requirements.text: The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Visual and tactile inspection of the outer surface; surface smooth and any protuberances do not hinder cleaning.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspection of the assembled lamp as mounted on the vehicle; inner (reflecting) surface of the retro-reflector is not accessible in normal use.

requirements.text: Retro-reflectors may consist of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, which must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Design review and manual separation attempt on retro-reflector with filter; optical unit and filter cannot be separated under normal use conditions.

requirements.text: The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
requirements.test_case: Material/process documentation review and inspection; colour obtained in the material (e.g. tinted plastic), no paint or varnish used.

requirements.text: For testing the night-time colour of white, red or amber retro-reflective devices, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric test set-up check: CIE Standard Illuminant A source, divergence angle 1/3°, illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or Annex 4, Part 1, para. 1.1 angle if a colourless surface reflection occurs); pass if the test geometry and illuminant conform.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of a white, red or amber retro-reflective device shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Illuminate with CIE Standard Illuminant A, divergence 1/3°, β1 = β2 = 0° (or Annex 4, Part 1, para. 1.1 angle); measure chromaticity x,y of reflected light with a spectroradiometer/colorimeter; pass if within the UN R48 night-time colour boundaries for the device colour (e.g. red).

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of shape and dimensions per Annex 5 on all ten samples; pass if all Annex 5 requirements are met.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 and colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. in the sequence of Table 4; pass if RI and colour limits of 5.1.4. and 5.1.5. are met.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
requirements.test_case: Run the physical/mechanical tests of Table 4 (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time, weathering); pass if each test and subsequent inspections are satisfactory.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. after each test group (trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt); pass if within R48 night-time colour limits.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have an RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Photometry per Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0° after each test group; pass if RI ≥ Table 3 value.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of Class IA and IB red retro-reflectors at angle of divergence α = 20' must be equal to or greater than 3.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 1.00∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
requirements.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at α = 20' at the three illumination angles; pass if RI ≥ listed values.

requirements.text: The RI values of Class IA and IB white retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than: at α = 20', 1.20∙103 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = β2 = 0°, 8.00∙102 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, 4.00∙102 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°; at α = 1°30', 2.0∙101, 1.12∙101 and 1.0∙101 mcd∙lx-1 respectively.
requirements.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4; pass if RI ≥ listed values for white.

requirements.text: The RI values of Class IA and IB amber retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than: at α = 20', 7.50∙102 mcd∙lx-1 at β1 = β2 = 0°, 5.00∙102 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, 2.50∙102 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°; at α = 1°30', 1.25∙101, 7∙100 and 6.25∙100 mcd∙lx-1 respectively.
requirements.test_case: Photometry per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4; pass if RI ≥ listed values for amber.

requirements.text: RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
requirements.test_case: Photometric scan within the bounded solid angle; pass if no RI below the applicable Table 3 values for β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0° and β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.

requirements.text: Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: If declared mounting height of H plane < 750 mm, limit downward photometric verification to 5°; pass if Table 3 values met in that range.
